newsitem.title: LATVIA: SHKELE TO PRESENT PLAN TO END GOVERNMENT CRISIS.
newsitem.headline: SHKELE TO PRESENT PLAN TO END GOVERNMENT CRISIS.

text.p: Latvian Prime Minister Andris Shkele said on Friday that next week he would announce a plan to end what he called a government crisis.
He said the government had been forced into problems by thoughtless statements by ministers and threats from political parties which he called "political blackmail".
"In reality, we are going through a government crisis," Shkele told a news conference.
"Next week, I will present a plan to the political parties on how to get out of this situation," he added.
He refused to give details on the measures that he would propose to end the crisis.
The multi-party government has been beset by problems over an anti-corruption which has caused the resignation of four government ministers.
Transport Minister Vilis Krishtopans has also been in the corruption spotlight but has refused to resign.
His party, Latvia's Way, has said that if Shkele makes Krishtopans quit, then it will leave the government.

Scandal has also arisen over a loan of eight million lats which was owed to bankrupt bank Banka Baltiya by state energy supplier Latvenergo but which was sold to a Lichtenstein financial firm for only five million lats.
An investigation has now been launched into the deal.
"I am filled with indignation about this agreement. I will do all that I can to make sure that this investigation is carried out energetically," Shkele added.
